free_text: The patient is a 65-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 4.53 and a biopsy-proven Gleason 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1) prostate adenocarcinoma with high-risk features. MRI demonstrates a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. The management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential treatment benefit against patient preferences regarding high-risk disease. The trade-off involves foregoing immediate treatment for observation versus proceeding with definitive therapy for a high-risk cancer.
